text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- All five opposition parties walked out of Parliament yesterday when their candidate for a seat on the Constitutional Court failed to receive the required number of votes. @
- Parliament yesterday passed bills lowering the average income tax, profit tax and consumption tax from next year.

- A senior official at the Ministry of Industry, Trade and Tourism said negotiations have so far failed to narrow the differing positions between Hungary and the World Trade Organisation on Hungarian agricultural export subsidies.
- The central budget had revenues of HUF 206 billion and expenditures of HUF 168 billion in October. @
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- Privatisation Minister Judit Csiha said she would discuss privatisation changes with the Free Democrats' parliamentary group next Monday.
- BorsodChem posted a pre-tax profit of 5.369 billion forints on sales of 30.487 billion at the end of September.
- The pharmaceutical company Egis closed August with pre-tax profit of 4.082 billion forints on sales of 17.3 billion forints. @
- Realbank will raise its 2.19 billion forints equity by at least 700 million forints and as much as 1.05 billion forints through a share issue.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- The junior coalition partner Free Democrats may head for a showdown with the Socialists when the future of social insurance is discussed in Parliament during today's special debate. @
- The Tiszai Chemical Works yesterday reported net profits of 6.912 billion forints, on sales of 45.7 billion in the first nine months of this year.
- Retail giant Fotex yesterday announced a convertible bond issue, available exclusively to current foreign shareholders of Fotex.
- Data regarding officially registered public companies is now available on the Internet through Internet Securities Hungary Kft. @
- An information system on waste management, set up with Swiss support, was presented to media representatives at the Ministry of Environmental Protection yesterday.
NEPSZAVA

- Executives of foreign energy companies that have invested heavily in the Hungarian energy sector are expected in Budapest in the middle of next week for talks with government officials on the postponed energy price hike. @

- President Arpad Goncz yesterday awarded the Medium Class Cross with the Star of the Order of Merit to Russian Ambassador Pavlovic Aboimov in recognition of his work in promoting Hungarian-Russian relations.
- A monitoring group from the United States, along with a group of French, Norwegian and Spanish supervisors, is overseeing the destruction of tanks in Godollo.
NEPSZABADSAG
- Croatian President Franjo Tudjman will visit Hungary November 22-23. @
MAGYAR NEMZET

- A senior police official said that Hungarian police learn of a crime in general being committed every 63 seconds, thefts are committed every 3.5 minutes and car thieves get away with stolen cars every 43 minutes.
-- Budapest newsroom (36-1) 327 4040
